artifact: SQLolla M0 instance viewer and AI explanation architecture review

reference.access: Official public repository read with the GitHub connector; relevant source and documentation inspected; no repository code executed or cloned
reference.reuse_boundary: Adopt architecture and interaction ideas. No source implementation copied. If later copying substantial code, preserve the MIT copyright and permission notice and review separately bundled dependencies. Its Python/Java application architecture does not replace SQLolla's Rust core.

findings.finding: The Java behavior engine invokes the Alloy API and extracts solver-owned instances. Its category enumerator returns up to three examples and records whether enumeration finished.
findings.adoption: Keep instance extraction inside the narrow Java Alloy bridge; Rust validates and stores a typed, immutable evidence envelope. Enumeration caps and completion status must remain visible.

findings.finding: Instance JSON contains traceLength, loopState, states with indexed signatures and ordered relation tuples, truncation and string-anonymization flags, and optional parameter bindings. The engine evaluates signatures and fields per trace state and preserves tuple column order.
findings.adoption: Use the basic states/signatures/relations structure, extended with stable source IDs, SQL types, row-occurrence identity, multiplicities, statement events and provenance.

findings.finding: The browser renders deterministic SVG from validated instance data, with exact tables, relation filtering and selection. Binary relations use arrows; higher-arity relations use ordered tuple markers. Isolated objects and repeated tuple positions are retained. The layout is a reading aid, not a semantic relationship.
findings.adoption: One immutable selected witness and state must drive graph, exact tables and transaction trace. Default SQLolla to business-table before/after views, with graph and raw Alloy data as complementary views.

findings.finding: Display limits and backend truncation are distinct. The diagram has default caps of 40 nodes and 48 tuples; exact tables describe returned data, which may itself already be truncated. Temporal examples have a state selector and an explicit loop note.
findings.adoption: Use separate fullEvidenceComplete, transportComplete and viewComplete flags and counts. A filtered or capped graph cannot support a claim that an omitted value is absent. A complete retained witness must remain available under the same evidence identity when claiming replayability.

findings.finding: Explanations accompany instances but do not generate their graph structure. The AI prompt forbids invented tuples/states and universal conclusions from bounded results. Chat reuses pinned current evidence and does not start another JVM; old-context responses are suppressed.
findings.adoption: Explanations are a separately validated annotation over solver evidence. Evidence IDs and current analysis revision must bind requests, responses and caches. Provider failure leaves the instance and deterministic explanation available.

findings.finding: AlloyStudio's four categories compare learner and oracle predicates: both accept, undercoverage, overcoverage and neither accept. They are not generic SQL security verdicts, and an entire-instance category does not identify one edge as the cause.
findings.adoption: SQLolla must derive witness labels from its own checked query intent and property evaluations. Do not reuse educational scores or infer that a highlighted row alone proves causality.

findings.finding: The reference supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and compatible-provider adapters, but credentials are private deployment configuration. Its learner browser explicitly does not accept provider keys or arbitrary endpoints; it is not a BYOT portal.
findings.adoption: SQLolla needs a distinct BYOT credential lifecycle and endpoint policy. Reuse the separation of provider adapters, local output validation, redacted errors and explicit provider choice, not the reference's credential UX.

rules: Only a concrete SAT assignment supplies an instance. UNSAT, UNKNOWN, timeout and error never receive invented graph or table data.
A satisfying instance satisfies the executed formula. It is not automatically a safe transaction. Display query intent, constrained properties and separately evaluated properties.
A property counterexample requires the validated violation-search formula and a witness of that violation; generic SAT is insufficient.
Before reporting no violation within bounds, check the scenario assumptions are satisfiable independently of the desired postcondition; expose inconsistent assumptions instead of vacuous success.
Keep assumptions, modeled SQL subset, atom/row/value/state bounds and arithmetic abstraction visible. No bounded result is labeled an unbounded proof.
The initial sequential transaction trace has no concurrency. Only display an Alloy temporal lasso or loop when the chosen model actually supplies one.

evidence_envelope_sketch.witness: null for statuses without a concrete assignment; otherwise immutable Witness

cells.value: typed value or explicit SQL NULL

witness_contract.loop_start_state_id: null unless a temporal lasso is actually modeled
witness_contract.parameters: typed bindings with explicit scope per statement/transaction
witness_contract.source_map: stable SQL statement/clause and RA node IDs to Alloy declarations/relations and evidence IDs; explicit coordinate units and missing-span markers
witness_contract.provenance: SQL, catalog/session, policy, parameter, IR and Alloy-model digests; parser/compiler/encoder/adapter/solver versions; scope; arithmetic/overflow policy; raw witness and redacted projection digests

viewer: Show graph, relational tables and ordered transaction trace for the selected instance; selections cross-highlight using stable IDs, never display-label equality.

Default nontechnical view shows affected business rows before/after, changed cells, returned rows, rollback/error outcome and the exact violated rule. Keep internal Alloy names in expandable technical detail.
SQL bags require row-occurrence identity or explicit multiplicity. Distinct equal-valued rows must not collapse merely because graph labels or cell values match.
Preserve tuple arity, position, direction, repeated endpoints and signature memberships. Distinguish NULL from missing data, empty string, anonymized value and truncation.
Treat labels and provider prose as literal text; no HTML/SVG interpretation. Provide keyboard selection, readable colors, accessible table equivalents and responsive behavior.
A highlight is an evidence locator. Claiming minimal causality requires a separate deterministic dependency or minimization result.
Retain the observed witness identity even when layouts change. SAT model enumeration may differ across solvers or runs; do not promise identical witnesses across environments.

ai_explanation.trigger: Explicit Explain action or explicitly enabled explanation as part of Analyze; changing graph selection or rendering alone causes no paid request
ai_explanation.input: Selected immutable evidence projection, current SQL/RA/policy source references, query intent, bounds, completeness, replay status and redaction metadata

output_sketch.proposed_changes: optional untrusted proposal requiring deterministic reanalysis

constraints: Every displayed factual observation must link to existing permitted evidence IDs; clicking a link highlights the exact row, tuple, state, property or source clause.
Reference validity is mechanically checkable; prose truth is not established merely because its citations exist. Display model-generated inferences distinctly and retain deterministic fact summaries.
AI cannot change solver status, witnesses, model provenance, policy truth, SQL-to-Alloy lowering or admission decisions.
Reject stale/mismatched/unknown evidence references and overlong or malformed provider output. Keep the original evidence visible if explanation validation fails.
Treat SQL identifiers, comments, row strings and user annotations as untrusted data, not model instructions. No tool execution or database writes are granted to the explanation path.

Cache by tenant/user, exact evidence projection digest, source revision, provider/account identity, model, prompt/schema version and relevant reasoning settings. Provider switching explicitly discloses selected context anew.
Token/provider failure, cancellation and timeout cannot suppress already validated solver results. Cancellation cannot recall data already sent to a provider.

byot: Implement a separate session-scoped credential handle; keys never enter the evidence JSON, LLM prompt, logs, exported artifact, URL or browser persistent storage.

Default to ephemeral server memory or an explicitly selected private-deployment secret store; redact errors and support revocation/expiry. Clearly disclose that the deployment backend receives the token when proxying provider calls.

Offer OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini through dedicated adapters. Compatible endpoints require a reviewed destination policy, HTTPS validation, redirect refusal and SSRF protection; do not expose unrestricted server-side fetch.
Keep provider/model/account selection explicit. No silent fallback or cross-provider resend. Show which redacted schema, query, witness and transcript fields will be sent.
Use provider-specific nonstorage options where available without claiming a universal provider retention guarantee. AI-disabled and offline deployments retain full deterministic viewing and analysis.

adversarial_acceptance_cases: SAT scenario that violates an unevaluated policy must not be labeled safe
UNSAT violation search under inconsistent base assumptions must not be labeled verified
Two equal-valued SQL row occurrences remain distinct in table/graph correspondence
Duplicate relation labels, repeated ternary columns, self-loops and isolated atoms preserve identity
Backend truncation, transport truncation, graph filtering and graph caps receive distinct notices
Cross-state IDs remain consistent; a finite SQL trace never acquires an invented temporal loop
HTML-like identifiers and prompt-injection strings render literally and cannot authorize actions
AI references an unknown or other-tenant tuple, stale revision or omitted state: reject annotation
Provider timeout/refusal/malformed response leaves the original instance usable
Provider switch, token expiry and compatible-endpoint redirects cannot leak credentials or silently change recipient
Keyboard-only and narrow-screen users can inspect exact tables and follow evidence links
Model/compiler/schema changes invalidate stale annotations while preserving historical source-bound evidence
suggested_plan_changes: Add an InstanceEvidence contract between Java bridge and Rust; keep raw solver data separate from validated SQL business projections and redacted AI projections.
Add an Instance Explorer frontend milestone covering table/graph/transaction-trace synchronization and exact-data export before AI polish.
Extend explanation contracts with instance/property/source IDs, revision freshness and citation validation; show a deterministic fact explanation when AI is unavailable.
Create separate delegated reviews for evidence extraction completeness, SQL row/multiplicity projection, visualization accessibility/security, and BYOT disclosure/freshness.
Include real SAT witnesses and intentionally absent witnesses in demonstration acceptance gates; avoid treating AlloyStudio's pedagogical comparison score as a SQL security score.
limitations: This is a source/documentation review, not an executed AlloyStudio test or deployment audit.
Reference documentation reports historical tests; those counts were not rerun and are not evidence for SQLolla.
The proposed data contract is architectural. No viewer, provider calls, UI or full witness extractor was implemented by this review.
Provider model catalogs in the reference were not independently verified and should not be copied as permanent SQLolla defaults.
